owner_name: Simon Sadler (via Blackpool Football Club Stadium and Property Ltd, inc. May 2019)
note: When Simon Sadler bought 96.2% of Blackpool FC from the receivers in June 2019 he separately bought the stadium, stadium property and training ground in a personal capacity; a separate company, Blackpool Football Club Stadium and Property Ltd, was set up in May 2019. It is not confirmed whether that company sits under the club company, so the ground may not pass automatically with the club.

lease_note: Rolling 7-year lease at a peppercorn rent (as reported)
note: The club bought the ground in 1933 and sold it to Luton Borough Council in 1989, leasing it back since. The club plans to move to a new 25,000-seat stadium at Power Court, approved December 2024, with piling under way by February 2026 and a target opening for 2028-29.

The council took the stadium back in 1980 and installed the club as tenant; the club rents it from the council and the two have jointly funded stand upgrades. There have been disputes over rent increases and funding for the North Stand, but no change of ownership found.

In December 2018 the club bought the freehold of the ground from Hyndburn Council for £400,000, ending about 50 years of leasing the land (it already owned the buildings). Owner Andy Holt put the club up for sale in October 2023 and an investment deal was reported later; no change to the ground's ownership was found.

Stadium references list the club as owner of Gresty Road, its home since 1906. A sale of a controlling stake was reported, but no transfer of the ground away from the club was found; freehold detail not confirmed from filings.

Stadium references list the club as owner of Blundell Park, its home since 1899. The 1878 Partners consortium (Jason Stockwood) bought the club from John Fenty in 2021 and has said a stadium move is not an immediate priority; earlier new-stadium plans involved council-owned land.

lease_note: Club holds a lease; terms not found
note: Sources conflict: stadium reference sites list Salford City FC as owner, but Place North West's 2024 coverage of the proposed AJ Bell Stadium swap (Salford Red Devils to take a lease at Moor Lane) describes the Peninsula Stadium as council-owned. The newer, more specific report is preferred; the club funded the rebuild of all four stands.

lease_note: Club is a tenant under a lease agreed with the council before the 2021 move; term not found
note: The £44m stadium opened in 2021, is owned by City of York Council and shared with York Knights and York Valkyrie rugby league. The club had to settle lease differences with the council before moving in from Bootham Crescent in January 2021.

Stadium references list Carlisle United as owner of Brunton Park, its home since 1909. The Piatak family's Castle Sports Group bought 90% of CUFC Holdings in November 2023 and is spending over £4.5m on the ground; no separate property company or lease was found.

The stadium and the wider Mill Farm sports village, opened in 2016, are owned by Tangerine Holdings, the Haythornthwaite family company; David Haythornthwaite also controls the club. It was not confirmed whether the club company sits inside the same group, so the ground may not pass automatically with the club.
